To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the immunosuppressive molecules are in the >10 kDa fraction of plasma and are not present in plasma of sham-treated rats.

plasma collected from rats 4 hr after a severe thermal injury (40% total body surface area) displays immunosoppressive activity (ISA) and that this ISA is associated with a window of immunodeficiency.

the plasma-mediated “window of immunodeficiency” in rats is a transient phenomenon that is temporally linked to the onset of cellular immune defects following trauma and stress, is functionally linked to these cellular immune defects, and is induced by a heat-labile molecule(s) in plasma that is >10-kD in molecular weight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the body's defenses are altered by injury and the mechanisms by which this is accomplished.
the identification of the etiology and mechanisms of immunodeficiency and the development of novel therapies.
the mechanisms by which trauma induces immunosuppression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a plasma-mediated window of immunodeficiency is induced in rats early following trauma and that these immunodeficiencies are temporally and functionually linked.
the etiology of the post-trauma immune defect is a plasma-mediated immunosuppressive factor(s) that is released into circulation early following injury.
plasma-mediated transient immunosuppression occurs following trauma and is associated with a similar decline in cellular immune function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system is compromised early following trauma and the mechanism for this is a plasma-mediated immunodeficiency.
the plasma-mediated window of immunodeficiency occurs in a time frame of approximately 1–8 hours following injury.
a 40% thermal injury to rats results in a transient, plasma-mediated, cellular immune dysfunction that is temporally and functionaly linked to a transient, cellular immune dysfunction in the rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a window of immunosuppression that occurs after a burn injury and this window is mediated by the plasma.
the immune system is compromised for 16–24 hr following trauma.
the immune system is suppressed in trauma patients for the first 24 hours following their injuries, and this suppression is caused by molecules in the blood plasma.
